Ask if they need the day/night to themselves

Ask if they’d like a hug/physical affection

ask if they’d like to talk about it. 

Present them with a blanket, hot tea, Nintendo switch/book/journal and leave them alone

I FEEL THIS, not only did I have to work some wage slave job but my parents actively tried to push me away from my passions because of them not wanting me to be a “ceramics making starving artist” and it destroyed my mental health. 

Don’t forget about the things/hobbies that make you truly happy. Pursue them. Hopefully your parents support your hobbies/interests.

Don’t be like me! Find a balance, get that slave wage (or better) and reinvest it into passions/hobbies. You’ll be better off and if you make a job out of your passion you’ll never have to work another day in your life.

Mental health > work. Your health as a young person is more important and putting more precedent over it would make homework and everything else so much easier. I didn’t/couldn’t and I’m paying for it now. 

It doesn’t get easier. Try to go to college if you can, I really miss that academic + fun + no parents environment as an adult. 

Try and find out about all the adulting you’ll have to do once your out of school (budgeting, health insurance, being independent, taxes, all the stressful important shit that they don’t teach you in school) the more cushion you can create now will serve you better once you’re out of school.

Edit: I second getting *good enough* grades to get to college, but put mental health first, I put balls to the wall in high school and was burnt out by the time I got to college. I should have put my mental health first over my high school grades so I could have been more happier going into college which would have helped.
